name: Private-sector DPRK IT-worker testimony in a congressional hearing

attribution.legal_posture: Official congressional hearing transcript recording private-sector witness testimony; it is non-binding testimony, while congressional finding, executive-agency determination, procurement rule and government or defense-contractor incident confirmation require separate evidence.

caveats: The cited figure counts incidents. Unique workers, employers, public-sector cases, and confirmed DPRK identities are separate questions.
Existing official and first-party controls provide stronger operational guidance; this record adds provenance and policy context rather than a new standalone screening control.
The record is limited to aggregate findings; person, entity, employer, victim, account, persona, image, identifier, and private-selector profiles require separate source records.
The official source establishes that the testimony occurred; DPRK-specific counts, characterizations, and recommendations remain claims by private-sector witnesses.
Testimony leaves any affected government agency, defense contractor, supplier, or other public-sector organization unspecified.

This is congressional-hearing context; Federal Acquisition Regulation provision, solicitation clause, contractor mandate, defense-industrial-base bulletin, and government-policy adoption status are unrecorded.

statements: At a January 22, 2025 House Homeland Security hearing, CrowdStrike's Adam Meyers testified that its managed threat-hunting service responded to 304 incidents in 2024 involving FAMOUS CHOLLIMA and characterized nearly 40 percent as insider-threat operations.

SentinelOne's Brandon Wales testified that DPRK IT-worker fraud remained active and framed enterprise HR teams as the first line of defense against false remote workers, with mules and laptop farms complicating detection before hiring.
limitations: The hearing date, witness identities, and text of their testimony are confirmed by the official transcript.

The transcript does not independently validate every underlying private-company incident or establish that any incident involved a public agency, government contractor, supplier, or defense-industrial-base organization.
The testimony may support future general hiring-security or insider-risk policy discussions, but it is not itself a rule, mandate, procurement requirement, or evidence that such a change is planned.

The hearing transcript contains no DPRK-specific Federal Acquisition Regulation change, solicitation clause, contracting-officer instruction, supplier-assurance mandate, defense-industrial-base bulletin, or identified government or defense-contractor victim.

sources.support: CrowdStrike witness Adam Meyers described North Korea's placement of malicious insiders in remote work positions and reported 304 2024 incidents involving FAMOUS CHOLLIMA, nearly 40 percent characterized as insider-threat operations. SentinelOne witness Brandon Wales separately stated that DPRK IT-worker fraud remained active, described HR as an enterprise front line, and discussed mules and laptop farms as pre-hire detection challenges
sources.locator: hearing pp. 8-11 and 23-24; PDF pp. 12-15 and 27-28
